cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: Sequential logic circuits have memory; their output depends on both current inputs and previous states.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: An SR latch (Set-Reset) is the simplest memory element, built from two cross-coupled NAND or NOR gates.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: The SR latch using NOR gates: S=1,R=0 sets Q=1; S=0,R=1 resets Q=0; S=0,R=0 holds state; S=1,R=1 is invalid.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: A D flip-flop (data) captures the D input value on the clock edge; Q follows D when clocked.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: A JK flip-flop generalises the SR latch: J=1,K=0 sets; J=0,K=1 resets; J=0,K=0 holds; J=1,K=1 toggles.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: The toggle feature of JK flip-flops (J=1,K=1) makes them ideal for building binary counters.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: Counters can be asynchronous (ripple) or synchronous; synchronous counters use a common clock for all flip-flops.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: An n-bit binary counter counts from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1 and then rolls over; a modulo-N counter resets after N.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: A shift register stores and shifts data left or right on each clock pulse; used for serial-parallel conversion.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: Flip-flops can be edge-triggered (responding to clock transitions) or level-triggered (responding while clock is high).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: A register file is a collection of flip-flops used to store multiple bits of data simultaneously.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Sequential Logic & Flip-Flops
cards.back: Timing diagrams show the relationship between clock, input and output signals over time.
